[1;97m5.1 — print-and-exit vs full-screen[0m

Most of the commands you've used print output and return immediately:
  [92mls[0m          [92mdate[0m          [92mwc -l file[0m

Other commands [91mtake over the screen[0m until you exit them:
  [92mman ls[0m              [90m# the manual page for ls[0m
  [92mless long-file.txt[0m  [90m# page through a long file[0m
  [92mvim file[0m            [90m# the Vim editor[0m

While one runs, the shell prompt is [36mgone[0m: you're inside a program,
and the same keys may do different things there.

[1;97m5.2 — entering and leaving Vim[0m

[92mvim[0m is a text editor. Before you [36medit[0m anything,
let's learn how to [36mleave[0m.

First, see if Vim is installed:
  [92mcommand -v vim[0m   [90m# a path means it is; if not, install it[0m

A safe entrance, then a full session with no file:
  [92mvim --version[0m   [90m# prints version info and exits[0m
  [92mvim[0m             [90m# leave with [0m[92m:q[0m[90m then Enter[0m

If Vim refuses (unsaved changes), use the [91mdiscard[0m form:
  [92m:q![0m then Enter

[91mYou will need :q![0m the first few times you use Vim. Memorize it.

[1;97m5.3 — buffer vs file[0m

[91mThe most important idea in this stage.[0m When you open a file in
Vim, Vim [36mreads it into a buffer[0m — a copy in memory. Your
keystrokes change the [36mbuffer[0m, not the file. The file on disk
only changes when you [36mwrite[0m the buffer back.

  [36mfile on disk[0m  →  [36mbuffer in memory[0m  →  [36mfile on disk[0m
       (read)                  (edit)                     (write)

That's why Vim has separate commands for save and quit:
  [92m:w[0m    write the buffer to the file
  [92m:q[0m    quit (only if there are no unsaved changes)
  [92m:q![0m   quit and discard unsaved changes
  [92m:wq[0m   write, then quit

[1;97m5.5 — calling vimtutor[0m

[92mvimtutor[0m is itself a shell command. It launches Vim on a [36mcopy[0m
of a tutorial file so you can practice without damaging the original.

Check whether it's installed:
  [92mcommand -v vimtutor[0m

If it prints a path, you're set. If not:
  - Linux: install your distro's full [36mvim[0m package (not [36mvim-minimal[0m).
  - macOS: [92mvimtutor[0m may not be on PATH; [92mbrew install vim[0m adds it.
